goal: Hook and the unit question: study Jacob Lawrence's Street to Mbari with its setting (Ibadan, Nigeria, 1964, the Mbari artists' club) and interpret how the people shown live and what they value.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Day 1 stays clean for the hook and the question: no readiness or retrieval task. Look-describe-interpret on the work card (described and linked, never copied); a return of the maker, a different work from the 3 to 5 band's. Sensitivity: the agent reads the museum's page and a source on the Mbari club first. Words met: interpret, value.

goal: Set up the year's studio routine and show value in graphite in named steps: a ten-step value scale with the step card, and open the one-week studio waste audit.
note: Processes: create; connect. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of comparing readings and finding cultural links (va-g5-look) and the practice log and care of tools (va-g5-craft), with the ten-minute reteach of the grade 5 log for a student new to the band. Set-up 4 minutes and clean-up 3 inside the 40. Waste audit session 1: the class logs scraps, rinse water and dried paint. Words: value, contrast, conserve.

goal: Show hatching, cross-hatching, stippling and blending in steps on practice strips, and take the baseline look at the unit's main look-for (a full value range).
note: Processes: create. Step card carried; baseline look in rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet, never scored. Audit session 2 logged at clean-up (one school week of audit). Pencil for every student; blending with a paper stump or a fingertip, hands washed.

goal: Read the week's waste audit together: tally it, explain how rinse water, scraps, dried paint and reuse affect the environment, and pick the one change the class will make.
note: Processes: create; connect. Opener: a five-minute value strip from day 3's steps. The change chosen (lidded rinse cups, a scrap box, reuse of one-sided paper) runs at every clean-up from here on. Words: conserve, reuse.

goal: Study a kente cloth woven by Asante weavers (Ghana) with its setting: what its pattern names and occasions of use show about how people live and what they value.
note: Processes: respond; connect. The unit plan picks the cloth from an open-access collection with its pattern names and occasions. Sensitivity: the agent reads a Ghanaian or museum source on the cloth's names and uses first; studied by looking, and no student copies a named pattern as costume. The day's evidence sentence uses interpret and points to the cloth.

goal: Show three new materials in steps (charcoal, ink wash, chalk pastel) on a material test sheet, with a log line for each on what surprised.
note: Processes: create. Free path: graphite worked three ways on card, newsprint and brown paper. Hazards and controls: charcoal and chalk pastel dust wiped with a damp cloth, never blown, pencil for a student with asthma; ink washable and non-toxic; rinse water in lidded cups; hands washed. Clean-up 6 minutes. Words: open, new method.

goal: Show still life drawing from observation in steps: the light source, cast and form shadows, sighting shapes, and the light block-in of a set-up.
note: Processes: create. Opener: value strip (five minutes). Each table has a still life of found objects under one light (a window or a desk lamp the teacher places; no student moves a lamp). The step card is withdrawn before the check, never before the second making day.

goal: Making day 1: draw the still life in value with the student's choice of objects and arrangement, carrying one material from the test sheet into it.
note: Processes: create. Daily evidence: the drawing in its current state and one line (the technique used, the change planned). The class's waste change runs at clean-up. Equipment: two pencils of different hardness, paper, a damp cloth for any dust.

goal: Study two posters of the federal Work Projects Administration (work safety and travel): mark the visual parts (value contrast, color, placement, lettering) and the cultural ties that steer a viewer, and say what each wanted people to do.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Public domain posters from the national library's poster collection; a return of the collection (the 3 to 5 band used one parks poster), with new posters on work safety and travel, none on disease. Words: persuade, contrast. Printed poster cards; the teacher screen only shows them.

goal: Value drills with partner feedback: match a printed value scale, shade a sphere three ways, and run one-minute stippling and hatching strips.
note: Processes: create. Practice of days 2, 3 and 7; nothing new. The partner names one look-for (value range or edge) in each round.

goal: Making day 2 with the year's first critique on the still lifes (describe, ask, suggest, tied to the value look-for), the teacher marking look-fors on the record sheet.
note: Processes: create; respond. Critique protocol returns from grade 5 as review. Praise alone is not feedback; each suggestion names a look-for. Collaborative talk practices SL.6.1 (not owned).

goal: Revise the still life after the critique and say in one line what changed; finish the material test sheet log and the waste-audit card (one environmental effect explained and the change made).
note: Processes: create; connect. Last making day: the test sheet with its log and the waste-audit card are kept and scored with the product (VA:Cr2.1.6a, VA:Cr2.2.6a). The still life goes into the portfolio folder with a one-line written reflection.

goal: Showing: hang the value still lifes with one-line notes in a hallway display, and each student writes one look-describe-interpret sentence on a classmate's drawing.
note: Processes: present; respond. Work goes outside the class only with the family's yes and under the student's chosen name. Tape or clips; anything above shoulder height hung by an adult.

goal: Study a work showing daily life in Oceania or Southeast Asia (the Candidate kept) for how people live and what they value, and practice the written look on it and on a new poster, partner-marked with the guide.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Candidate kept: one day inside the unit's 16. The unit plan picks an open-access work with its maker, place, date and purpose. Practice only, nothing scored.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check on the guide, then written items on an unseen work from another part of the world (VA:Re7.1.6a) and an unseen public domain poster (VA:Re7.2.6a); the test sheet, log and waste card are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: respond; create. Check day minutes: set-up and settling 3, self-check 5, written sitting 27, collecting 3, 2 to spare; no paint, ink or print. Each part of each code has its own prompt (VA:Re7.2.6a: one visual part, one cultural association, how each steers, what it wants). Any item may be answered aloud at the teacher's table. Response time: day 16.

goal: Respond day: a second try at each part marked not yet, in groups from the record sheet (at most four), the others extending their still life.
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (the test sheet, log and waste card); responding (the written look). Starts from the marks taken after day 15.

goal: Hook and the unit question: study a Juanito Laguna collage by Antonio Berni with its setting (Buenos Aires, 1960s, scrap gathered in its poor neighborhoods) and how he turned a concern into a work.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Day 1 stays clean: no readiness or retrieval task. Described and linked to the holding museum's page. Sensitivity: the agent reads the museum's page first; Juanito is an invented boy, and no student is asked about their own family's money or home. Words: inquiry, concept.

goal: Show the idea swap in steps, then run it in groups of three: each writes two concepts and the group joins them in pairs into fresh ideas, credited to the group on idea pages.
note: Processes: create. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of merging ideas and choosing a research method (va-g5-ideas) and the artist statement (va-g5-revise), with the ten-minute reteach for a student new to the band. Sketchbook model returns. One student at home: the parent is the group's second member.

goal: Show color schemes (complementary and analogous) with the color wheel step card, and paint collage papers in one scheme.
note: Processes: create. Paint premixed and water-based; covered tables; brushes washed; the class's waste change from unit 1 runs at clean-up (6 minutes). Free path: old calendars, newspaper and scrap paper sorted into a scheme. A color-scheme practice tool or its printed wheel.

goal: Color scheme drill: paint or sort a second set of papers in the other scheme, and a partner checks each against the printed wheel.
note: Processes: create. Practice of day 19. Baseline look at the main look-for (the collage's parts carry the meant idea) taken here on the papers' first arrangements, rotating groups.

goal: Study Mark Bradford's collage of paper gathered from city streets (sources gathered from a place), then show the planning page: a question, two sources and a first sketch that follows from them.
note: Processes: respond; create; connect. Described and linked; the unit plan records whether the maker is living, as of its date. A public or invented topic is offered beside a personal one and marked the same. Words: source, inquiry.

goal: Gather the two sources (a look, a short interview or a reading) and complete the planning page with a first sketch that follows from them.
note: Processes: create. A question about a worry is handled with health's steps if a student tells something. The planning page is kept for the look-for (VA:Cr1.2.6a).

goal: Study Henri Matisse's The Snail (Tate, 1953) for cut and arranged painted paper, and show collage in steps: tearing against cutting, layering and glue control.
note: Processes: respond; create. Described and linked. Scissors; glue sticks and white glue, no spray adhesive; hands washed. Step card carried.

goal: Collage drills with partner feedback: torn and cut edges, glue control, and layering papers in three values.
note: Processes: create. Practice of days 19 and 23, with unit 1's value contrast in the layering. Opener: a two-minute check of the class's waste change.

goal: Making day 1: build the collage from the planning page in the chosen color scheme.
note: Processes: create. Daily evidence: the collage in its current state and one line. Scissors, glue, painted papers; free path papers.

goal: Making day 2 with the critique: a partner retells what the collage says before the maker explains (describe, ask, suggest), and the teacher marks the record sheet.
note: Processes: create; respond. The retelling card is the viewer's step; the maker listens first. Talk-about-choices and critique-protocol models return. Words: viewer, intent.

goal: Revise the collage: compare the retelling with what was meant, change the work to match, and log the change on the record sheet.
note: Processes: create. Word: revise. The change and its reason are what the day-31 item asks about.

goal: Finish the collage and write the artist statement that compares what was meant with what the viewer saw; portfolio piece with a one-line reflection.
note: Processes: create. Writing day, so Application. The statement is carried into the showing.

goal: Showing: the collages with their statements, for a partner class, whose students retell one collage each before reading its statement.
note: Processes: present; respond. Family yes and chosen name for any showing outside the class. One student at home: the family is the partner class.

goal: Practice for the mid-year check, nothing scored: a timed value strip and a paired look at a new poster's visual parts and what it wants a viewer to do.
note: Processes: create; respond. Retrieval of unit 1 seven weeks after its end (week 8 to week 15); practice, never check evidence. The value strip uses graphite only, so the check's new dry material stays unseen. Dropped on the once-a-week path and on the 10-days-short year (unscored; its codes are taught on other days), never folded into a check.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check, then a written item on the student's own revised collage (what was meant, what the viewer saw, the change and why); the idea pages and planning page are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: respond; create. Check day minutes as day 15. VA:Cr3.1.6a item checked against the record sheet; VA:Cr1.1.6a look-for: at least two fresh ideas joined from group members' concepts, joining shown; VA:Cr1.2.6a look-for: question, two sources, a sketch that follows. Response time: day 32. This record is carried unscored into the mid-year check.

goal: Respond day: a second try at the parts marked not yet (a clearer joining of ideas, a source added, the change explained).
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (idea pages, the planning page and the statement). Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the others pair on a second idea swap.

goal: Year 6 mid-year check (course-level, week 17): a short value study in a dry material not used in unit 1 (VA:Cr2.1.6a) and written items on an unseen work from another part of the world (VA:Re7.1.6a) and an unseen poster's visual parts, one cultural association and what it wants (VA:Re7.2.6a).
note: Processes: create; respond. Right after unit 2's end-of-unit assessment, so its items draw on unit 1 only; unit 2's record (day 31) is carried unscored. New tasks: the unit 1 items were given on day 15, nine weeks before; day 31's form (a written item on the student's own work) is not repeated. Minutes as the check day: 3, 5, 27 (the value study and two written items), 3, 2. School day 83, week 17: no core check in grades 6 to 8 that day; health checks on day 84.

goal: Respond to the mid-year check: a second try at the parts marked not yet, the others taking the value study further.
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (the value study); responding (the written look). Groups from the record sheet, at most four.

goal: Hook and the unit question: study Inuit snow goggles with their setting (the Arctic, carved wood or bone, narrow slits against snow glare) as a design that meets its users' needs.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Day 1 stays clean: no readiness or retrieval task. Sensitivity: the agent reads the museum's page and an Inuit organization's or maker's published words first; the student's model is their own design, never a copy of an Inuit object. Words: user, need.

goal: Study the sidewalk curb cut won by disability rights activists in Berkeley in the early 1970s, and show the user interview card and the design brief.
note: Processes: respond; connect; create. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of labeled sketches of places and objects (va-g5-design) and judging across cultures with a standards set (va-g5-judge), with the ten-minute reteach. Sensitivity: told through the activists' own published words; no student is asked about a classmate's disability or health; user cards include invented users with stated needs.

goal: Build the class idea wall: the teacher first gathers four ideas aloud on the collection card (shown, thinking each through), then each student gathers at least four ideas from current interests and worries that art-making could explore, marks how art could explore each, and picks a design problem.
note: Processes: connect; create. Public or invented ideas count the same; health's steps if a student tells something. The collection card is kept (VA:Cn10.1.6a). The teacher shows the gathering before anyone gathers alone, so VA:Cn10.1.6a is not first met in independent work.

goal: Interview two users (a classmate, a family member or an invented user card) and write each user's stated needs on the design brief.
note: Processes: create; connect. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of unit 2's planning page and the partner's retelling as an intent check (va-g6-ideas, va-g6-revise), before the interviews. Design-brief model returns. One student at home: a parent and an invented user.

goal: Show cardboard construction in steps: scoring with a blunt tool, folding, tab and slot, and joining with tape and glue; take the baseline look at the main look-for (each need met by a part of the model).
note: Processes: create. Hazards and controls: cardboard cut by an adult only with a blade; students use scissors; scoring with a blunt tool; tape and glue. Free path: cereal boxes, tape and glue. No scale drawing asked.

goal: Construction drills with partner feedback: a scored fold, a tab-and-slot joint and a small test box.
note: Processes: create. Practice of day 39's steps.

goal: Study Amrita Sher-Gil's Three Girls (India, 1935): sort context cards into useful and unhelpful, then use subject, form, structure and media to find its ideas and mood.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Opener: a two-minute look-describe-interpret warm-up on the work (unit 1's routine). Described and linked. Words: context, mood.

goal: Making day 1: build the model for the named users' needs from the brief.
note: Processes: create. Daily evidence: the model in its current state and one line. Adult cuts only.

goal: Show how to create criteria for judging a work and the evidence sentence (a judgment and the part of the work that shows it), then use them on Sher-Gil's painting.
note: Processes: respond. New model: evidence-sentence. Lean: ELA grade 6 unit 2 teaches argument writing (school days 33 to 58), before this day; the criteria sheet still gives the frame and the teacher models one judgment, and the item scores the criteria and the evidence, never the writing conventions. Words: criteria, evidence.

goal: Making day 2 with the critique: partners judge each other's models with their own criteria in evidence sentences (describe, ask, suggest).
note: Processes: create; respond. Teacher marks the record sheet against the look-fors.

goal: Opener (10 minutes): partner-marked practice on a second work card, context cards sorted and its idea and mood found (VA:Re8.1.6a practice, nothing scored). Then revise the model after the critique and write the design note: each named user's need and how the model meets it; portfolio piece with a one-line reflection.
note: Processes: create. Writing day, so Application. The model and note are kept for the look-for. The opener practices day 41 on a second work, so the scored item on day 47 is not the first unaided try.

goal: Showing: a user fair for the users interviewed or a partner class, where visitors use one criterion and an evidence sentence on a model.
note: Processes: present; respond. Family yes and chosen name for a showing outside class.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check, then written items on an unseen work with six context cards (VA:Re8.1.6a) and criteria written for it with a judgment in evidence sentences (VA:Re9.1.6a); the idea collection and the model are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: respond; create; connect. Check day minutes as day 15. VA:Re8.1.6a prompts each part: useful cards kept, one unhelpful set aside with a reason, then idea and mood from subject, form and media. Response time: day 48.

goal: Respond day: a second try at the parts marked not yet (a need met, a context card sorted, an evidence sentence rewritten).
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (a need met in the model); responding (a context card sorted, an evidence sentence rewritten); connecting (the idea collection). Groups from the record sheet, at most four.

goal: Hook and the unit question: study the cave paintings of Lascaux and the painted pig of Leang Tedongnge (Sulawesi) with their dates and the dating method, and how the earliest art shows its era, materials and uses.
note: Processes: connect; respond. Day 1 stays clean: no readiness or retrieval task. Dates and claims only as the site and the 2021 study state them. Lean: social studies grade 6 unit 2 (school days 11 to 25) has taught early humans; the work cards still give each work's date, the dating method in one sentence and its place. Words: era, preserve.

goal: Compare how flat, three-dimensional and digital art are kept and shown (light, handling, mounts, file care) on a three-column chart.
note: Processes: present. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of the curator's argued choices (va-g5-show) and evidence from a real exhibit (va-g5-museum), with the ten-minute reteach. Digital work on printed screen cards; no device per student.

goal: Study the Ah-Tah-Thi-Ki Museum of the Seminole Tribe of Florida from its own pages: how it mirrors its community's history and values, with a work card for each work, and Seminole patchwork as art changing with new materials.
note: Processes: present; connect; respond. Sensitivity: the agent reads the tribe's museum pages first; the removal wars are told in the museum's own words; no student copies a patchwork design. Candidate kept at no day cost: the pages are checked open and free on the day the unit plan is written, a local museum's pages named as the alternative. Words: community, display.

goal: Show mounting on card and labels (title, maker, date, medium) in steps, choose the portfolio pieces from units 1 to 3, and take the baseline look at the main look-for (a display plan that weighs space, viewers and layout).
note: Processes: present. Mount card cut by an adult or with scissors; glue sticks; tape. Free path: cereal-box mounts, painter's tape.

goal: Mounting and label drills with partner feedback: margins by eye, a label in the set order, a straight hang with tape; then ten minutes partner-marked on the three-column chart for a second set of a flat, a 3D and a digital work (VA:Pr4.1.6a practice, nothing scored).
note: Processes: present. Practice of days 50 and 52; the chart practice keeps the day 61 item from being the first unaided try.

goal: Show the display plan drawn as a wall elevation (not to scale): weigh the space, the viewers (eye level, path) and the layout.
note: Processes: present. Words: display plan, layout, viewer. Exhibit-plan model returns.

goal: Draw the display plan, alone or in a group, for the hallway or a classroom wall from the year's kept work.
note: Processes: present; create. Create here is real making: the display plan is drawn as a design for its viewers and checked on unit 3's design-brief look-for (each viewer's need named and met), practice of VA:Cr2.3.6a that returns, never a claim. Daily evidence line: what technique I used and what I will change, with the plan in its current state.

goal: Write the source-based response: a claim on how the Seminole museum (or a local one) mirrors its community's history and values, with two pieces of evidence on work cards.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of the planning page and criteria with an evidence sentence (va-g6-ideas, va-g6-judge), ahead of the year-end check. The response is kept and scored (VA:Pr6.1.6a). Evidence-sentence model returns.

goal: Critique of the display plans (describe, ask, suggest, tied to space, viewers and layout), and trace one change in art across eras (cave pigments, patchwork on new machines, a digital work) on a sort card.
note: Processes: present; connect; respond. Teacher marks the record sheet.

goal: Revise the display plan after the critique, then mount and label the chosen works and finish the source-based response.
note: Processes: present. Last making day for the kept plan and response.

goal: Hang the show from the plans, checking eye level and the viewers' path.
note: Processes: present. Students hang on the floor and at reach with tape or clips; anything above shoulder height hung by an adult; no ladders for students.

goal: Showing: the year-end hallway show for families, students guiding visitors; portfolio piece with a one-line reflection.
note: Processes: present; respond. Shown outside the class only with the family's yes and under the student's chosen name.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check, then written items on an unseen flat, 3D and digital work in the three-column chart (VA:Pr4.1.6a) and two unseen works from different eras (VA:Cn11.1.6a); the display plan and source-based response are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: present; connect; respond. Check day minutes as day 15. VA:Cn11.1.6a prompts each part: era, custom, materials and use. Response time: day 62. This record is carried unscored into the year-end check.

goal: Respond day: a second try at the parts marked not yet (a column of the chart, a weighed choice on the plan, a second piece of evidence).
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: presenting (a column of the chart, a weighed choice on the plan, a second piece of evidence); connecting (an era, custom, material or use read). Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the show is taken down after.

goal: Year 6 year-end check (course-level, week 32): a new planning page for a question the student picks from three given ones or writes as their own, marked the same (VA:Cr1.2.6a: content that matters to the student and a chosen approach, each prompted), and on one unseen work, context sorted with its idea and mood (VA:Re8.1.6a) and a judgment against the student's own criteria (VA:Re9.1.6a).
note: Processes: create; respond. Right after unit 4's end-of-unit assessment, so its items draw on units 2 and 3; unit 4's record (day 61) is carried unscored. Week 32 is the finals week (CALENDAR.md rule 3). Minutes as the check day.

goal: Respond to the year-end check: a second try at the parts marked not yet; the portfolio folders go home with their reflections.
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (the planning page); responding (context, idea and mood, and the judgment). Groups from the record sheet, at most four.

goal: Hook and the unit question: study the cast brass plaques of the Kingdom of Benin in three settings (palace pillars, museum cases abroad after 1897, returned to Nigeria from 2022) and how display, place and experience change how they are seen and valued.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Day 1 stays clean: no readiness or retrieval task. Sensitivity: the agent reads the museum's pages on the 2022 return and a Nigerian museum body's published words first; the 1897 taking is told plainly as the museums tell it; objects made for royal ancestral altars are studied by looking only and never imitated. Words: display, location.

goal: Reopen the studio routine and show washes in steps: a flat wash and a graded wash with the step card.
note: Processes: create; connect. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of interpreting how people live and how images sway (va-g6-look) and the environmental cost of supplies (va-g6-craft), with the ten-minute reteach for a student new to the band. Rinse water conserved as in unit 1. Water spills wiped at once; brushes washed; clean-up 6 minutes. Free path: graphite joined with layered found-paper collage, secured by folds or tabs.

goal: Study Fan Kuan's Travelers among Mountains and Streams for ink built up in layers, show wet into wet and dry brush, and take the baseline look at the main look-for (controlled layers).
note: Processes: respond; create. From the holding museum's open data images. Words: layer.

goal: Wash drills with partner feedback: flat, graded, wet-into-wet and dry-brush swatches.
note: Processes: create. Practice of days 66 and 67.

goal: Show ink line over a dry wash, plan the long piece (the student's own subject), and open the process log.
note: Processes: create. Ink water-based and non-toxic. Practice-log model returns as the process log across sessions. Word: persist.

goal: Session 1 of the long piece: first washes, with a log line on what was tried and fixed.
note: Processes: create. Daily evidence: the piece in its current state and the log line.

goal: Study Norman Rockwell's Freedom of Speech (1943) as a magazine painting and then a war bond poster: several ways one image sways particular audiences.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Opener: wash swatch (five minutes). Described and linked. The unit studies persuasion, not a war's rights and wrongs. Word: audience.

goal: Session 2 with the critique: describe, ask, suggest on the half-made pieces, tied to the layers look-for.
note: Processes: create; respond. Teacher marks the record sheet.

goal: Session 3: revise after the critique and log what was fixed.
note: Processes: create.

goal: Wash and line drills with partner feedback: line weight with the ink, a graded wash over a dry layer.
note: Processes: create. Practice of days 66 to 69.

goal: Session 4 of the long piece, in two media, with the log line.
note: Processes: create. Four sessions now logged, the look-for's floor.

goal: Show the duty to self and others when sharing images online: permission, no faces or names, the caption, who may see it.
note: Processes: create; connect. Nothing is posted; no student makes an account or photographs a face. Words: permission.

goal: Session 5: finish the piece, write the sharing plan for a photo of it (kept card), and put the piece in the portfolio with a one-line reflection.
note: Processes: create. Last making day: the piece, the process log and the sharing plan card are kept and scored.

goal: Showing: the finished pieces with their process logs in the classroom; viewers read one log and name one fix.
note: Processes: present; respond.

goal: Study a work by a living maker shown both online and in a gallery (the Candidate kept): how the two displays change how it is seen and valued, and what sharing it asked of the maker.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Candidate kept: one day inside the unit's 18. Described and linked; the unit plan records whether living, as of its date.

goal: Practice the written look, partner-marked with the guide: one work in two settings, and one poster for two audiences.
note: Processes: respond. Practice only, nothing scored. Dropped on the once-a-week path and on the 10-days-short year (unscored; its codes are taught on other days), never folded into a check.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check, then written items on an unseen work in two settings (VA:Re7.1.7a) and an unseen public domain poster for two audiences (VA:Re7.2.7a); the piece, log and sharing plan are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: respond; create. Check day minutes as day 15. VA:Re7.1.7a prompts display, place and experience apart. Response time: day 82.

goal: Respond day: a second try at the parts marked not yet (a session's fix logged, a duty explained, an audience named).
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (a session's fix logged, a duty explained); responding (a setting or an audience named). Groups from the record sheet, at most four.

goal: Hook and the unit question: study Gustave Caillebotte's Paris Street; Rainy Day (1877) with its setting, and how a stated aim (a street that reads as deep) shapes a work.
note: Processes: respond; connect. Day 1 stays clean: no readiness or retrieval task. Open access image. Words: aim.

goal: Show one-point perspective in steps from a Curio Class original diagram: horizon line, vanishing point, lines to the point, a box; take the baseline look at the main look-for (lines meet at the point).
note: Processes: create. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of the planned inquiry (va-g6-ideas) and intent against a viewer's retelling (va-g6-revise), with the ten-minute reteach. Rulers or a card edge; points sharpened by the teacher or with a hand sharpener; no blades. Word: vanishing point.

goal: Perspective box drills with partner feedback: boxes above, below and on the horizon line.
note: Processes: create. Practice of day 84. A perspective guide tool or its printed grid.

goal: Show a street or room in one-point perspective, then compare that simple construction with Caillebotte's street and with a Persian or Mughal painting's own space system (the Candidate kept).
note: Processes: create; respond; connect. Candidate kept at no day cost: ten minutes of this day. The unit plan picks an open-access painting with its maker, place, date and purpose.

goal: Study Sol LeWitt's wall drawings, made by others from his written instructions, for how written rules shape a work; write three or four criteria the student's perspective work must meet for its stated aim.

note: Processes: present; create. Writing day, so Application. Create here is real making: the introduction panel is laid out on unit 11's pictures-and-words grid and checked on its look-for (the message reads first), practice of VA:Cr2.3.8a that returns, never a claim. Daily evidence line: what technique I used and what I will change.

goal: Critique of the stories and the hang plan (describe, ask, suggest, tied to the viewer look-for).
note: Processes: present; respond. Opener (10 minutes): retrieval of criteria on unfinished work and the argued judgment (va-g8-revise, va-g8-judge), ahead of the year-end check. Teacher marks the record sheet.

goal: Revise the stories after the critique and hang the show.
note: Processes: present. Work hung with tape or clips by students at reach; anything above shoulder height by an adult; no ladders for students.

goal: Showing: the year-end themed show for families and the school; visitors leave notes; portfolio piece with a one-line reflection.
note: Processes: present; respond. The visitors' notes are read in the last ten minutes for what the show did to visitors' thoughts (VA:Pr6.1.8a practice). Family yes and chosen name for every work shown.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: self-check, then written items on an unseen exhibition on a Curio Class card (why it may influence visitors, how, and its effect on thoughts, beliefs and experience; VA:Pr6.1.8a) and four unseen works sorted by how each serves a group's identity (VA:Cn11.1.8a); the jury card and the showing are scored from the kept work.
note: Processes: present; connect; respond. Check day minutes as day 15. VA:Pr5.1.8a look-for on the showing: the student's part of the hang and the story they wrote. Response time: day 190. This record is carried unscored into the year-end check.

goal: Respond day: a second try at the parts marked not yet (a criterion applied, a story rewritten, a sort reason given).
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: presenting (a criterion applied on the jury card, a story rewritten, the influence item); connecting (a sort reason given). Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the show is taken down after.

goal: Year 8 year-end check (course-level, week 32): in a 10-minute item, two criteria applied to a new unfinished Curio Class original and two changes planned (VA:Cr3.1.8a); in a 17-minute item, a short argued paragraph on a new unseen work: a claim, two reasons each with evidence that names the work's subject, form or media (this evidence carries VA:Re8.1.8a), and one counterclaim answered (VA:Re9.1.8a).
note: Processes: create; respond. Right after unit 12's end-of-unit assessment, so its items draw on units 10 and 11; unit 12's record (day 189) is carried unscored. Unit 11's argued judgment was given on day 177, seven weeks before. Finals week. Minutes: set-up 3, self-check 5, sitting 27 (10 + 17), collecting 3, 2 to spare; the items are sized to the sitting, not to day 177's whole-sitting model, and are new items on a new work.

goal: Respond to the year-end check: a second try at the parts marked not yet; the band's portfolio folders go home with their reflections.
note: Respond day; processes of the parts redone: creating (criteria and changes on the unfinished work); responding (the argued judgment and its evidence). Groups from the record sheet, at most four.
